item.claim: At baseline 75% of the children in this study attained the recommended 60 min of daily MVPA and MVPA was significantly associated with two motor competence components.
item.label: supported
item.originalClaim: At baseline 75% of the children in this study attained the recommended 60 min of daily MVPA and MVPA was significantly associated with two motor competence components.

result.quote: Almost three-quarters of preschoolers (n = 439/588, 74.7%) reached recommended levels of MVPA per day when ankle placement cut points were applied. ... Object control, locomotor scores, and GMQ were not associated with minutes of MVPA/day in unadjusted or adjusted linear models. In multivariable logistic regression, increased GMQ was associated with slightly increased odds of meeting MVPA guidelines (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.00, 1.09) (Table 3). This was driven by object control which was positively associated with meeting MVPA guidelines (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.19). Locomotor was not associated with meeting MVPA guidelines in unadjusted or adjusted models.
result.reason: The source supports that 74.7% reached recommended MVPA levels, but it does not support a significant association with two motor competence components: object control was associated with meeting guidelines, whereas locomotor was not; the other association was with the gross motor quotient, a composite measure.
